chunks: The right of the offering (hady) is that you desire God through it, and do not desire His creation through it; you desire through it only to be exposed to God's mercy and the deliverance of your spirit on the day you encounter Him.

key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: The ritual offering, typically an animal sacrificed during Hajj or for specific devotional purposes.
key_terms.يَوْمَ تَلْقَاهُ: The day you encounter Him (God), referring to the Day of Judgment.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual purpose and right of the ritual offering (hady) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In the context of Imam Zayn al-Abidin’s Risalat al-Huquq, this definition elevates the ritual offering (hady) from a mere physical act to a profound exercise of monotheistic intentionality (ikhlas), ensuring the deed is not diluted by worldly motives. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the inner state of the worshipper, where the primary objective is securing divine mercy and the ultimate salvation of the soul upon meeting God. This reflects the broader jurisprudential principle that the validity of acts of worship depends heavily on the purity of the heart's intent.
